stories.h: State lawsuit payouts on pace for another record year
stories.s: Washington paid a record $537 million to settle claims last fiscal year and is tracking toward nearly $600 million now. Ahead of the January session, a study panel floated damage caps and a victims' fund.

stories.h: UW and Harborview staff walk out over pay offer
stories.s: SEIU 925 members walked off the job at UW campuses and Harborview. The union says the university's final offer has no raises, and 83% of members rejected it. UW says it has asked for state mediation.

stories.h: Measles spreading in WA as US loses elimination status
stories.s: Washington has had roughly five times as many measles cases this year as in all of 2025. The state health officer warns exposure is possible anywhere, and some kindergarten vaccination rates are near 50%.

stories.h: US 101 on Hood Canal reopens after overnight mudslide
stories.s: A mudslide near the Hamma Hamma area in northern Mason County shut both directions of US 101 early Wednesday. WSDOT reopened one lane by late morning and all lanes shortly before 2 p.m.

talking.h: Will the Sonics return? NBA expansion decision nears
talking.s: NBA Commissioner Adam Silver wants an expansion decision by the end of 2026. Seattle and Las Vegas lead the field, and Kraken owner Samantha Holloway's group is heading Seattle's bid.

talking.h: Seattle's Hey Bagel wins six awards at New York BagelFest
talking.s: The University Village shop took first place for best sourdough bagel and earned five other honors in New York. A West Seattle location is planned for 2027.

talking.h: Cathay Pacific to fly Seattle–Hong Kong daily
talking.s: Starting March 28, 2027, Cathay Pacific will fly its Sea-Tac to Hong Kong nonstop daily instead of five times a week. It is the only nonstop between the Northwest and Hong Kong.

coming.h: King tides arrive as Ocean Shores rushes repairs
coming.s: Ocean Shores is under a state of emergency, with crews placing riprap to shore up storm-damaged shoreline before the season's first king tides arrive.

coming.h: Thanksgiving-week razor clam digs open at Copalis, Mocrocks
coming.s: WDFW approved five evening digs from Nov. 24 to 28, including Thanksgiving Day. Long Beach and Twin Harbors stay closed because of domoic acid. Diggers 16 and older need a license.
